thesis.title: Did passive investing lead to higher abnormal returns?
thesis.abstract: We show that the large increase in the share of passive funds did not lead to an increase in mutual fund abnormal returns. On a panel of roughly 30,000 U.S. equity funds, we find no relationship between the passive share and fund alpha. This result is robust to subsample analysis and consistent with the extension to achievable alpha. Our findings are consistent with the Berk-Green mechanism of fund-manager competition rather than the price discovery of Grossman-Stiglitz.
